place_fields.vibe: riverine wilderness, dry deciduous forest and adventure
place_fields.summary: A large protected landscape along the Cauvery River in Karnataka, noted for riverine habitats, wildlife, birdwatching and permitted adventure activities such as trekking and rafting.

planning_attributes.description: Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary spans the Cauvery river corridor across parts of Mandya, Chamarajanagar and Ramanagara districts and supports diverse dry deciduous, thorn and riverine habitats.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: The sanctuary has a broad elevation range; Ponnachi Betta is among its high points.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Established in 1987 as a wildlife sanctuary and subsequently expanded; it is named for the Cauvery River that runs through the protected landscape.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Road access is available from Karnataka towns including Kanakapura; tourism facilities and activity bases include Bheemeshwari, Galibore and Doddamakali.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Wildlife activities and angling require applicable permits/bookings; access can be restricted according to forest and wildlife-management rules.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Use authorized guides/operators for forest and river activities, follow wildlife regulations, and exercise caution around river currents and remote forest terrain.
planning_attributes.notes: Known for grizzled giant squirrel habitat, mahseer fish and more than 200 recorded bird species; rafting, coracle rides and trekking are offered in designated areas.

place_fields.summary: A major tiger reserve in southern Karnataka forming part of the Nilgiri Biosphere landscape, with rich populations of tigers, elephants and other wildlife and established safari tourism.
place_fields.best_time: October to February for cooler weather and good visibility; March to May can also provide strong wildlife-viewing opportunities.

planning_attributes.description: Bandipur Tiger Reserve lies in Mysuru and Chamarajanagar districts and forms an ecological link with adjoining protected forests in Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: The reserve occupies the foothills and surrounding landscape of the Nilgiris; its terrain includes dry-deciduous forests and scrub.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: The forest was historically a Mysore Maharaja game reserve, became a Project Tiger reserve in the 1970s and is part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: Bandipur is on the Mysuru-Ooty highway and is accessible by road from Mysuru, with safari operations from designated forest and tourism facilities.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Entry and safari movement are controlled by the forest authorities; jeep and bus safaris operate in designated time slots and areas.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Do not leave designated vehicles or approach wildlife; follow safari staff instructions and forest rules, especially around elephants and predators.
planning_attributes.notes: The reserve is recognized by NTCA as a tiger reserve with a core area of 872.24 sq km and total tiger-reserve extent of about 1456.3 sq km.

place_fields.micro_region: Mudumalai Tiger Reserve, Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu
place_fields.vibe: Nilgiri forest, elephant corridor and tiger habitat
place_fields.summary: A protected forest landscape on the northwestern Nilgiris at the Karnataka-Kerala-Tamil Nadu junction, known for elephants, tigers, gaur, leopards and rich birdlife.
place_fields.best_time: Year-round for general visits; early morning and late afternoon are especially suitable for wildlife viewing.

planning_attributes.description: Mudumalai Tiger Reserve occupies the Nilgiris landscape in Tamil Nadu and connects ecologically with protected areas in Karnataka and Kerala.
planning_attributes.elevation_or_height: The reserve lies on the slopes of the Nilgiris and descends toward the Mysore plateau; the core area covers 321 sq km.
planning_attributes.legend_or_history: Part of the forest has been protected since 1940; it became part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve in 1986 and was declared a tiger reserve in 2007.
planning_attributes.how_to_reach: The reserve straddles the Mysore-Ooty interstate highway and can be approached from Mysuru or Ooty; Theppakadu is a principal visitor and safari base.
planning_attributes.access_restrictions: Safaris and other visitor activities are subject to Forest Department rules, designated areas and booking/permit requirements; timings can vary seasonally.
planning_attributes.safety_notes: Stay with authorized safari operations, follow forest instructions, and maintain safe distances from wildlife; forest roads can be steep and conditions can change with weather.
planning_attributes.notes: The core/critical tiger habitat is 321 sq km and the notified buffer adds 367.586 sq km, for a total tiger-reserve area of 688.586 sq km.
